newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property stocks slammed by government comment.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks slammed by government comment.

text.p: Property stocks fell on Monday on fear of possible government controls on the local property market after Financial Secretary Donald Tsang expressed concern over the recent surge in property prices, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Properties sub-index fell 1.20 percent by midday compared to the main index's 0.43 percent slide.

"Comments by Donald Tsang has given the market an excuse to sell down the property stocks," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage. "However, I see a psychological effect on the property market rather than an actual impact...I don't really expect any actual intervention in the market."

Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said he had assigned a team to study the recent surge in property price and will pay attention to speculative acitivities if they affect the livelihood of the territory's citizens.

Shares of Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd fell HGK$1.75 to HK$94.75 at midday, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd was down HK$1.50 to HK$74.50, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.50 to HK$66.50 and New World Development Co Ltd down HK$0.10 to HK$49.10.
Brokers said concerns over U.S. interest rate trends also triggered selling on the interest rates sensitive stocks.
